description: source_citation backfill for the controls topic, from the 2026-07-30 adversarial sweep (docs/question-verify/controls-batch-*.md). Only the 13 items with a provision a reviewer quoted verbatim are listed — the other 24 are technique with no statutory basis and must stay NULL. A blank citation is the honest answer; a stretched one destroys the audit trail.

ops.why: reg 308(1)(f): a driver shall not 'allow such vehicle to remain unattended on such road without setting its brake'. Legislation — the provision is the rule tested.
reg 326(1)(a) requires the driver to 'signal his or her intention to turn or move to the left or right by operating the direction indicator'. Legislation.
reg 203 requires a wiper that will 'wipe the outside of the windscreen directly in front of the driver'. Legislation — the 'outside' is exactly what the item turns on.

The item is about demisting the INSIDE, for which no provision exists. reg 203 corroborates only the explanation's side-claim that wipers clear the outside. Marked corroborating so the field cannot be read as making demisting statutory.

reg 150 requires a motorcycle to have 'two independent braking systems' and sets a combined-efficiency standard. It supports the premise that there are two brakes; it does NOT legislate using both to stop, which is K53 technique. Corroborating, not the source.

reg 198(6)(a) permits simultaneous indicators when the vehicle is 'stationary in a hazardous position' or 'in motion in an emergency situation', and (b) forbids them 'in a circumstance other than those referred to'. Legislation — the keyed answer nearly quotes it.

reg 157(3): a driver 'shall extinguish the main-beam … if such main-beam could cause a dangerous glare to oncoming traffic'. 157(1)(b) carries the 150 m visibility rule that kills the lights-off distractor. Legislation.

reg 326(1)(a) is unconditional, which is what makes the 'only if another vehicle is near' distractor legally wrong rather than merely poor practice. regs 324/325 supply the 'before reaching the point' timing. Legislation.

reg 310A confines hooter use to compliance with the regulations 'or on the grounds of safety' — the stem's 'warn of danger' maps onto it directly. reg 201(1)(a) requires the device to be fitted and audible at 90 m. Legislation.
reg 1 defines a stop lamp as signalling 'the intention of the driver … to stop or reduce the speed'; reg 168(1) requires them at the rear. Legislation.
Same provision as VC-008 and again on point: the wiper clears the outside of the windscreen, which is where the rain is. Legislation.

The item bundles seat, mirrors and belt. Only the belt has a provision — reg 213(4). Seat and mirror adjustment are technique. Qualified in the field so the citation is not read as covering the whole answer.

reg 1 makes keeping the vehicle stationary the parking brake's ordinary-course purpose, which is what refutes the 'only for emergencies' distractor; reg 155(1)(c) sets its gradient-holding standard (1 in 8,33). The hill-start half of the answer is technique, so the citation is corroborating.
